$comment: The permissions this software enforces, the roles it ships with, and which
permission each route requires. Applied by `brain migrate up`.
This file is the product's defaults, not the last word. The database is the
source of truth at runtime, so an enterprise creating its own roles and
granting them from a dashboard needs no deploy. The loader reflects that:
permissions  upserted. Never deleted — an enterprise may have granted
one, and the foreign key would refuse anyway.
roles        only the ones named here are touched. A role created by an
operator is never modified or removed.
routes       replaced wholesale. Routes come from code, so this file is
authoritative and a row for a route that no longer exists
is stale rather than someone's configuration.
Startup compares the mux against `routes` and refuses to serve when a
protected route has no entry. A missing mapping is a crash naming the
route, never a silently open endpoint.

permissions.name: user:read
permissions.description: Look people up by name or subject

roles.name: admin
roles.description: Full access within a team, including membership

roles.name: member
roles.description: Create and change agents and tools within a team
